briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Tax Pressure, Bigger Wins: Michigan Brands Expand as Federal Cannabis & Psychedelic Policy Advances
briefs.top: Michigan operators are finding real daylight even as the 24% wholesale tax bites — a homegrown brand is scaling nationally, prices are stabilizing, and both governor's-race candidates are now talking relief. Nationally, courts and the FDA keep pushing cannabis and psychedelic policy forward, from a preserved medical rescheduling win to Trulieve's NYSE debut and Compass Pathways gearing up for a psilocybin launch.

local.text: Michigan-born JARS Cannabis scales up out west — The East Detroit-founded chain is acquiring Sonoran Roots' eight Ponderosa dispensaries, creating a 27-store network that becomes Arizona's largest cannabis retailer.

GOP nominee courts the cannabis vote on tax relief — John James has pledged to repeal or sharply cut Michigan's 24% wholesale tax and picked up the state cannabis industry's endorsement, while Democrat Jocelyn Benson takes a wait-and-see stance.

Muskegon's Fields Cannary preps a dispensary-restaurant hybrid — The hospitality-forward buildout is targeting a fall opening, pushing Michigan's retail format further than most stores in the state have gone.
Flower prices stop climbing after tax-driven spike — The average ounce dipped to $59 in April from $62 in March, a sign the market is adjusting to the new levy rather than collapsing under it.
New dispensary blooms in downtown Ann Arbor — Blue Sky Cannabis Co. quietly opened next to Spores Cafe, adding fresh competition and foot traffic to the city's core.

national.text: Compass preps workforce for psilocybin's market debut — The company tapped therapy-training firm Fluence to build standardized provider education ahead of a potential FDA approval for its COMP360 psilocybin therapy.
FDA finalizes the rulebook for psychedelic drug trials — New guidance covers psilocybin, LSD and MDMA study design and paired with a September public hearing on therapeutic use.

Federal court keeps medical marijuana's Schedule III move intact — The D.C. Circuit declined to stay the reclassification, meaning medical cannabis stays Schedule III while opponents' lawsuit plays out.

Trulieve lands on the NYSE in a historic first — The multistate operator restructured into a 100% medical footprint to complete the major-exchange listing under ticker TRLV following federal Schedule III reclassification.

DEA's own brief says weed doesn't belong in Schedule I — The administrative judge still hasn't ruled after 11 days of hearings, but the agency's post-hearing filing concluded cannabis no longer meets the statutory criteria for the top tier.
